items.reason: Pinning a tag to a commit SHA means asking GitHub what that tag points at right now and this session has no network; the repository already ships the one-command close (`npm run actions:pin`, which resolves every ref AND writes STRICT=true + RATCHET.pinned back into scripts/actions-pin.mjs in the same pass), so there is nothing useful to add offline and inventing SHAs would break the workflows rather than pin them.

A budget that fails a build needs a recorded ceiling, and every candidate number (route First Load JS from .next/app-build-manifest.json, a Lighthouse score, a bundle byte count) requires running `next build` or the app — this session cannot execute anything, so any budget file I wrote would carry invented ceilings and would be a gate that is green by exemption, which is the exact shape this repository already calls out in scripts/actions-pin.mjs.

A maintainer labelling an issue `agent:draft` now fires .github/workflows/issue-dispatch.yml, which asks a model for a change and opens a DRAFT pull request against the existing gates; the proposal may only write src/, test-unit/ and docs/, the model key and the write scope are in separate jobs, and the dispatch announces its own absence when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY lapses.

Mutation testing is a measurement — the deliverable is a survivor list for the chokepoint modules and a threshold derived from it — and it requires running the 475-file unit suite once per mutant; this session has no shell, so I could ship a harness but not a single measured survivor, and a mutation gate with no baseline measures nothing.

`fix: Top priority` passed every rule in scripts/commit-subject.mjs — twelve characters, two words, conventional shape, no narration vocabulary — so rubric A5 had nothing to block it with; the new `queue-position` rule refuses a description made entirely of a rank word plus a filler noun, anchored to the whole description so the vocabulary stays usable in real subjects.

lessons: This repository enforces its workflow-security rules from BOTH sides: scripts/actions-pin.mjs is the gate and test-unit/workflow-injection.test.mjs independently re-asserts the same invariants, and one of them (`every ${{ … }} must sit inside an env: block`) rules out job-level `outputs:` entirely — cross-job values have to be re-derived from $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH in each job rather than passed. Read those two files before adding any workflow here.

Any new key-gated workflow step must be declared in scripts/harness-degradation.mjs CAPABILITIES and must call `--announce <id>` on both branches of its `if [ -z "$KEY" ]`; `harness:degradation:check` goes red on a `secrets.NAME` no capability declares, and the drill inside the unit suite proves the announcement actually appears.

When a rule exists and the thing it targets is still in the history, check first whether the rule actually MATCHES the escaped example before adding enforcement paths — here the gate ran everywhere it needed to (pre-push, every push, every PR) and the only gap was the rule's own vocabulary.
